name: Le Royal Monceau - Raffles Paris
positioning: Historic Paris hotel on avenue Hoche reinterpreted by Philippe Starck, with an art gallery, a private cinema and a Michelin-starred Italian restaurant
best_for: Art and design lovers who want a gallery, an art collection and a private cinema in the hotel
Food-focused travelers drawn to a Michelin-starred Italian restaurant and a Starck-designed brasserie
Travelers who want a base a few steps from the Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Elysees

facts.text: The hotel is at 37 avenue Hoche, a few steps from the Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Elysees, close to Parc Monceau.
Since 1928 the hotel has had close ties with artists and writers of Parisian cultural life.
Raffles Spa & Wellness was designed by Philippe Starck.
The spa offers treatments from Dr. Barbara Sturm, 111Skin and Nooance.
Il Carpaccio's menu was created in partnership with Da Vittorio restaurant in Brusaporto.
Il Carpaccio opens onto a glass conservatory filled with natural light.
Le Bar Long is a Parisian brasserie designed by Philippe Starck, set around a long table and serving reinvented French classics from breakfast through dinner.
Le Bar Long has live music every Thursday.
La Cuisine serves breakfasts and a Sunday Royal brunch.
The hotel has a cigar lounge dedicated to Havana and Montecristo cigars.
The Royal Film Club holds a monthly gastronomic experience during film screenings at the Katara cinema.
Suites combine 1940s and 50s design with poetic details such as books on the shelves and a message scrawled on a lampshade.

highlights.text: The hotel is a historic landmark reinterpreted by French architect and designer Philippe Starck.
The hotel has a contemporary art gallery, a collection of more than 300 works, the Librairie des Arts bookshop and an Art Concierge.
The Cinema Katara is a private 99-seat auditorium that hosts Royal Film Club screenings and events.
Il Carpaccio earned its Michelin star again in 2026.
The Ray Charles Suite, Suite 714, displays snapshots of Ray Charles and has a Pleyel piano.

considerations.text: Allow around 45 minutes from Roissy-Charles-de-Gaulle and Orly airports.
WhataHotel notes the contemporary, art-focused design may not appeal to travelers who prefer traditional luxury.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's premium positioning.
